concepts.action: Keep the short native candidate and the SymPy spelling at the adapter boundary; decide whether any Fortran alias is needed.
concepts.description: Create one named symbolic expression.
concepts.finding: The native Fortran facade uses the concise internal name sym. The Python surfaces use SymPy's Symbol spelling.

concepts.action: Document one canonical native behavior and keep SymPy shape adaptation in the Python layer.
concepts.description: Create several named symbols.
concepts.finding: The same spelling crosses the Fortran and Python convenience surfaces, but the accepted syntax and return shape differ.

concepts.action: Retain both by layer and test the mapping.
concepts.description: Create an exact integer.
concepts.finding: num is concise and native. Integer is the compatibility spelling.

concepts.action: Retain both by layer and test the mapping.
concepts.description: Create an exact rational.
concepts.finding: rat is concise and native. Rational is the compatibility spelling.

concepts.action: Retain the disambiguating native pair and keep Float as an adapter alias.
concepts.description: Create a real expression.
concepts.finding: The native facade keeps _expr on value and text constructors because the suffix distinguishes expression handles from intrinsic scalar values. The adapter has one SymPy-compatible Float constructor.

concepts.action: Document the ownership distinction and avoid a second public concept unless the argument distinction is observable.
concepts.description: Create an applied or named function.
concepts.finding: func and func_in are internal/native entry points with different argument ownership. Function is the compatibility spelling.

concepts.action: Keep the elementary functions as one native family and do not reintroduce per-function aliases.
concepts.description: Create an elementary applied function.
concepts.finding: The Fortran facade uses the same intrinsic spellings as fortsym_expr. The Python adapter preserves SymPy spellings while covering the declared elementary-head subset.

concepts.action: Keep complex-domain algebra in one owner. Do not add native re/im aliases or duplicate projection logic in the adapters; translate only the SymPy spellings at the boundary.
concepts.description: Project supported expressions into real, imaginary, modulus, conjugate, or principal-argument form.
concepts.finding: The native facade keeps explicit snake_case names that describe the operation and its expression-valued result. The Python adapter uses SymPy's compatibility names and routes the supported complex-domain work to fortsym_complexdom, falling back to an unevaluated Abs head when reality is unknown.

concepts.action: Keep one native constructor family and the SymPy spelling at the adapter boundary; retain suffixes where they distinguish expression sentinels from other native names.
concepts.description: Create standard named constants.
concepts.finding: Native names describe expression constructors, including the explicit sentinel suffixes. Python compatibility names follow SymPy's capitalization and infinity spelling.

concepts.action: Keep partial and diff in the calculus owner, with the facade forwarding evaluated differentiation consistently.
concepts.description: Differentiate an expression.
concepts.finding: partial constructs an explicit unevaluated node; the easy facade's diff uses the native evaluated operation. The Python layer keeps SymPy's diff and Derivative boundary.

concepts.action: Keep one responsibility per owner and document default versus explicit state once.
concepts.description: Own expression storage and expression handles.
concepts.finding: Fortran types and Python handle classes are distinct language bindings. The default-state functions have no direct SymPy root equivalent, and the native facade uses short names because its module already supplies the namespace.

concepts.action: Keep one native context owner; close compound facts transactionally and expose compatibility names only in the adapter.
concepts.description: Query and scope supported expression assumptions.
concepts.finding: The native facade owns value-style contexts and sign facts while the adapter keeps SymPy's Q/ask/assuming/And vocabulary at the Python boundary.

concepts.action: Keep structural substitution in fortsym_subs, expose only its concise single-pair and explicit paired-sequence spellings from the native facade, and keep xreplace, replace, exact match, and Wild at the SymPy adapter boundary.
concepts.description: Replace expressions.
concepts.finding: The native facade forwards both substitution shapes from the single owning module; the Python adapter applies SymPy's unordered mapping order and maps the simultaneous, exact-node, exact-replace, exact-match, and bounded Wild remainder/partition boundaries.

concepts.action: Keep one native engine owner and expose the concise transformation names from the easy facade.
concepts.description: Transform an expression algebraically.
concepts.finding: The Python adapter exposes the native transformation subset. The Fortran convenience facade forwards the transformations to the native engine with one optional status convention, and refine names the assumption-aware entry point while the simplifier owns guarded rewrites.

concepts.action: Keep the tree traversal in the native arena owner and expose only spelling adapters at the language boundaries.
concepts.description: Count operation occurrences in an expression tree.
concepts.finding: The native facade names the scalar structural query operation_count; the Python compatibility layer preserves SymPy's count_ops spelling while visual operation expressions remain outside the bounded subset.

concepts.action: Keep free-symbol discovery in the existing fortsym_eval traversal and expose only collection and spelling adapters at the boundaries.
concepts.description: Return the distinct free symbols of an expression.
concepts.finding: The native facade uses the concise free_symbols name, the native Python facade exposes the same top-level helper, and the compatibility Expr property reuses the same C-ABI traversal owner.

concepts.action: Keep one relation recorder in fortsym_assume; expose compatibility spellings only at the Python adapter boundary and refuse unsupported relation inference explicitly.
concepts.description: Construct symbolic equality and ordering relations.
concepts.finding: The Fortran facade keeps relation constructors snake_case. The Python adapter preserves SymPy's constructor spellings and maps comparison operators to the same native relation nodes.

concepts.action: Keep them out of the SymPy adapter unless a defined SymPy behavior exists.
concepts.description: Inspect handle validity and arena ownership.
concepts.finding: These are native safety predicates with no Python compatibility spelling.

concepts.action: Keep zero_test as the only user-facing zero query and reuse the engine verdict constants rather than adding check_* sisters.
concepts.description: Ask whether an expression is zero without guessing.
concepts.finding: The native facade has one zero query with TRUE, FALSE, and UNKNOWN outcomes. Assertion and numeric-probe helpers remain in fortsym_check.

concepts.action: Keep numeric-expression classification in fortsym_predicates and do not duplicate it in the C ABI or Python adapter.
concepts.description: Ask whether an expression is numeric.
concepts.finding: The native predicate owner classifies numeric atoms and numeric-only compounds once; the compatibility adapter preserves SymPy's boolean Expr.is_number spelling.

concepts.action: Keep exact-domain classification in fortsym_predicates and do not duplicate it in the C ABI or Python adapter. Keep Q.algebraic dispatcher-only adjustments at the compatibility edge.
concepts.description: Ask whether an expression is algebraic.
concepts.finding: The native predicate owner classifies the supported exact algebraic fragment once; the Python adapter preserves SymPy's tri-state Expr.is_algebraic spelling.

concepts.action: Reuse one result type across facade operations and zero queries instead of adding operation-specific status vocabularies.
concepts.description: Return one common result for native expression operations.
concepts.finding: The easy facade and native engine share engine_result_t for expression values, success, verdicts, timings, and diagnostics.

concepts.action: Keep them in a numeric module with one naming family.
concepts.description: Evaluate or inspect numeric values.
concepts.finding: These are fortsym-specific inspection and callback concepts, not SymPy root aliases.

concepts.action: Keep them behind their owning verification/backend modules.
concepts.description: Record backend proof and equivalence evidence.
concepts.finding: These are fortsym verification and code-generation concepts with no SymPy facade equivalent.

concepts.action: Keep node-kind vocabulary private or in the representation owner unless consumers need it.
concepts.description: Inspect and identify native DAG node kinds.
concepts.finding: These are representation-level native tags with no SymPy facade equivalent.

concepts.action: Keep the exact-domain constructors under one documented native vocabulary and avoid duplicate aliases for the same domain.
concepts.description: Construct exact text, algebraic values, or named constants in the native arena.
concepts.finding: exact, algebraic_expr, and const are concise native constructors. They cover distinct exact domains and overlap only at the deliberate constructor boundary.

concepts.action: Keep one concise pair for string construction and extraction; do not add symbolic string aliases.
concepts.description: Convert between Fortran character values and the native string wrapper.
concepts.finding: str and chars are language-boundary helpers owned by fortsym_string, not symbolic operations or SymPy compatibility names.

concepts.action: Keep code-generation names together under the kernel owner and expose no duplicate backend-evidence aliases.
concepts.description: Describe and emit generated Fortran kernels.
concepts.finding: The kernel specification, emitter, and mode constant form one native code-generation vocabulary with no current SymPy root alias.

concepts.action: Keep one operator family and document assignment as symbol construction only.
concepts.description: Use Fortran operators and character assignment for the default facade.
concepts.finding: Operators and assignment are language syntax, not named SymPy functions. They belong to the native facade consistency audit.

concepts.action: Keep protocol constants in the backend owner and do not mirror them into the symbolic facade.
concepts.description: Represent backend protocol versions, statuses, and serialized evidence.
concepts.finding: These names describe fortsym's verification protocol and have no SymPy root equivalent.

concepts.action: Keep it in the calculus owner until its SymPy parity contract is defined.
concepts.description: Solve the native ODE fragment.
concepts.finding: solve_ode is a native specialized operation with no current Python or SymPy adapter entry.

policy.fortran_facade: short native names are audited as the canonical candidates
policy.python_facade: fortsym's native Python binding is audited separately from the SymPy spelling adapter
policy.selection: This report records the selected native vocabulary and the deliberate Python compatibility boundary.
policy.sympy_adapter: fortsym.sympy uses SymPy names where compatibility requires them
